clue.text: How much is taken from slipshod sea dog?

indicators.note: slipshod means careless and untidy, so the letters that follow are put back in a sloppy new order

parts.note: the six letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A careless old sailor wondering how much rum he has had.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosage is the measured quantity of a medicine a patient takes at one time.

clue.text: Boring wrestling manoeuvre results in stalemate

parts.note: dead means dull or lifeless, as in a dead party
a lock is a hold that pins an opponent's limb

explanation.surface: A dull wrestling hold leaves neither fighter able to win the bout.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock is a standstill where neither side can make progress, the same idea as a stalemate in chess.

clue.text: Swimmer sculls up and down fluidly, ignoring slight hiccup at first

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to scull is to row a boat
D is the standard abbreviation for down

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of each of the four words before it

parts.note: the initials of the four words

explanation.surface: A rower moves smoothly along the river, untroubled by a small hitch at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up and down' reads like a description of rowing, but it splits: 'up' turns the rowing word over, and 'down' is just D.
explanation.definitionFit: A swordfish is a large ocean fish with a long flat bill, and any fish is a swimmer.

clue.text: Good old Nell only half dead

indicators.note: keeping only half of the name means dropping its second two letters

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
O is the abbreviation for old
the name taken as written

explanation.surface: A sad report that dear old Nell is barely alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone is a gentle euphemism for having died.

clue.text: Winner gets 9 points and loser 5 in this game?

definitions.text: Winner gets 9 points and loser 5 in this game?

parts.note: surface reading: a match report where one player beats another by nine points to five
setter's reading: the words themselves are scored, since in this board game each letter tile carries a value, and the letters of the two words add up to those totals

explanation.walkthrough: In the board game each tile scores: W is 4 and every other letter of the two words is worth 1, so the six-letter word totals 9 and the five-letter word 5.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble is the word game where players score by the printed points on their letter tiles.

clue.text: Mismanaging slight income — lush's last to leave when the pubs kick out

indicators.note: mismanaging something handles it badly, so the letters get jumbled out of their order
to leave means that letter departs from the collection before it is rearranged

parts.note: the twelve letters taken as written

indicators.note: last asks for only the final letter of the drinker's word

parts.note: a lush is a heavy drinker; its final letter

explanation.surface: A drunk who has squandered a small wage has to leave when the pub shuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the H from the twelve letters, then rearrange the remaining eleven. In Britain pubs traditionally called last orders and closed at a fixed hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Closing time is the hour at which a pub stops serving and customers must leave.

clue.text: She's caught in a deceit

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the cricket letter inside the falsehood

parts.note: a lie is a deceit
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A woman has been exposed in a deception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She's' reads as 'she is', but the 's is just a link: 'She' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice is a woman's name, so it stands for 'she' as an example.

clue.text: Give a lift to old love in one hour from Greenwich?

indicators.note: in places the two round letters inside the time-zone abbreviation

parts.note: British Summer Time runs one hour ahead of Greenwich Mean Time
O is the abbreviation for old
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Helping an ageing sweetheart with a journey across a single time zone.
explanation.walkthrough: BST, British Summer Time, is the UK's clock in summer, an hour ahead of GMT.
explanation.definitionFit: To boost is to raise or encourage, as in giving someone's spirits a lift.

clue.text: Oddly easy to articulate 25 pieces of prose

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in the first, third and other odd positions

parts.note: first and third letters
to say something is to articulate it

explanation.surface: An instruction that some answers are simple to put into words.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 refers to the answer at 25-down, SMALL, so the definition reads 'small pieces of prose'.
explanation.definitionFit: Essays are short written compositions on a single subject, the typical small piece of prose.

clue.text: Volume of band on radio unacceptable — about eleven in the end

parts.note: AM is a radio waveband, amplitude modulation

indicators.note: about means the word for unacceptable goes around that final letter

parts.note: out means not allowed, as in that's out

indicators.note: in the end asks for only the final letter of the number word

parts.note: final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Complaints that a radio station's music is too loud, around eleven at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' wants to mean loudness in this radio picture, but it means quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Volume in the sense of quantity, as in a large volume of mail, is an amount.

clue.text: 15 20 conference — one with many frequent flyers?

parts.note: the UN climate change summits are called COP, Conference of the Parties
I is the Roman numeral one
lots means many

explanation.surface: Delegates jet in to a climate summit, many of them notorious air travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 20 points to the answer at 15 and 20 across, CLIMATE CHANGE. 'Frequent flyers' looks like air-mile collectors; it is the definition of people who fly planes for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: Co-pilots are the second pilots in a cockpit, so they fly very often as their job.

clue.text: See 5
Cover over pool

parts.note: a lid covers a container
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A tarpaulin stretched across a swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool.

clue.text: Drill bit used regularly, calmly and with attention to detail

indicators.note: used regularly means only letters at even intervals are taken, every other one

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters
gently means calmly

explanation.surface: A craftsman uses a drill steadily and carefully on fine work.
explanation.definitionFit: Working diligently means working with care and steady effort, giving close attention to detail.

clue.text: Shower curtain not cut

indicators.note: not means the three letters named next are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
the letters to remove, taken as written

explanation.surface: A bathroom shower curtain left at full length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower curtain' reads as one bathroom object; it splits into the definition and the word to be trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A shower is a brief fall of rain.

clue.text: Can Michael get around existential crisis?

indicators.note: to get letters around is to move them about into another arrangement

parts.note: the thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man named Michael can overcome a crisis about the meaning of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Existential crisis' usually means a personal crisis about meaning; here it is a crisis that threatens existence.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate change is often described as an existential threat, one that endangers human existence itself.

clue.text: Turn unknown informant in empty garage

indicators.note: in places the unknown and the informant inside the shell of the building
an empty building has no contents, so only its outer letters remain

parts.note: first and last letters
y is an unknown quantity in algebra
a rat is someone who informs on others

explanation.surface: Handing over an anonymous grass in an abandoned garage, like a crime drama scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to turn round and round, revolve or spin.

clue.text: Folk dance recital unaffected

indicators.note: a recital is a spoken performance, so it is the sound of the word that counts

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance

explanation.surface: A natural, unpretentious performance of folk dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone real is genuine and natural, without pretence, which is what unaffected means.

clue.text: Starts to tearfully recite Buddhist mantra over remains — they're in the pit

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so only the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: the opening letters
om is the sacred syllable chanted in Buddhist and Hindu meditation
bones are a person's mortal remains

explanation.surface: A mourner chants a mantra over a body buried in a grave.
explanation.walkthrough: The pit suggests a grave in this funeral scene; it is the orchestra pit below a theatre stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Trombones are brass instruments played by musicians seated in a theatre's orchestra pit.

clue.text: Lied about head's inaction

indicators.note: about suggests moving the letters around into a different order

parts.note: rearranged
a ness is a headland or promontory, as in Orford Ness

explanation.surface: Someone lied about their boss doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is the state of doing nothing, a lack of activity or work.

clue.text: See 15
Cleaned, tidied and covered in doilies?

indicators.note: tidied means rearranged into order, so the letters are shifted about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A house-proud host prepares the table with lacy mats.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: doilies are made of lace.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlaced means wrapped or decorated with lace, and doilies are small ornamental lace mats.

clue.text: Jewel cleaner put back on side of dresser

indicators.note: put back means the word is written from its end to its start

parts.note: a maid is a household cleaner
taken as written

indicators.note: a side is an edge, so only the first letter of the furniture word

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A cleaner returns a precious stone to the edge of a dressing table.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond is the most prized of precious stones, a jewel.

clue.text: Party guys on vacation — they go where they like!

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, so only the outer letters stay

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: Holidaying partygoers who roam wherever they please.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: dogs famously relieve themselves wherever they choose, and 'go' is a euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogs are notorious for fouling anywhere they please, a joke on the euphemism of going to the toilet.

clue.text: Material in half a brick

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: running across the gap between the words

explanation.surface: Building material found within half a brick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' tempts a solver to halve a word; it simply supplies letters for the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric is cloth or textile, the material clothes are made of.

clue.text: Message lab about a number of things

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: the ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A note from the laboratory about several items.
explanation.definitionFit: An assemblage is a collection or gathering of several things together.

clue.text: Poky numismatist's centre with everything under sun

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the following pieces below the abbreviation for sun

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun

indicators.note: centre asks for only the middle letter of the coin collector's word

parts.note: the sixth of eleven letters
all means everything

explanation.surface: A coin collector's cramped room crammed with everything under the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: A numismatist is a coin collector. 'Everything under the sun' is a stock phrase, but here 'under' places pieces beneath S.
explanation.definitionFit: A poky room is cramped and tiny, so poky is a synonym for small.

clue.text: Ultimately storm surge bent 'indestructible' weather gauge

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of each word is wanted

parts.note: the final letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A storm surge buckles a supposedly unbreakable weather instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weather gauge' reads as one instrument, but 'weather' gives a letter and 'gauge' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A meter, in the American spelling, is a measuring instrument or gauge, like a gas meter.

clue.text: Gifted rare type of claret by the French

parts.note: claret is slang for blood, and AB is the rarest blood group
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A talented connoisseur picks out an unusual French red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is a Bordeaux red wine, and in British slang for blood, which is the sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gifted is talented and capable, which is what able means.

clue.text: Wicked Bard has sent up Liberal

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Bard is the setter's pseudonym, so 'Bard has' is I've, as the setter would say it
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A cruel playwright has mocked a Liberal politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bard usually means Shakespeare, but here it is the setter talking about themselves, a common crossword device.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked and evil are synonyms for morally bad.

clue.text: Great tache! Trim sides and stick back on

indicators.note: trimming the sides cuts off the letter at each end, leaving the inner run

parts.note: the letters inside, running across the gap between the words

explanation.surface: Admiring a fine moustache, then trimming it and gluing it back on like a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: A tache is British slang for a moustache.
explanation.definitionFit: To reattach something is to fix or stick it back on again.

clue.text: Hail recent broadcast for traditional approach to country houses

parts.note: ave is Latin for hail, a greeting

indicators.note: broadcast means transmitted to listeners, so the sound of the word is used

parts.note: recent means new

explanation.surface: Cheering a new radio programme about stately homes.
explanation.walkthrough: An avenue originally meant a tree-lined drive leading up to a country house, before it came to mean a town street.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional sense of an avenue is a tree-lined approach road to a large country house.

clue.text: State maybe red according to its residents — all despite Obama's leadership

parts.words: maybe red according to its residents
parts.note: red is an example of a colour, spelt the American way as its residents would

indicators.note: leadership asks for the leading, first letter of each word

parts.note: the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A US state may vote Republican red even though it backed Obama.
explanation.walkthrough: Red is the colour of Republican states in US politics, which gives the surface its sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Containers of flavourful Assams and kombuchas?

indicators.note: taken with 'Containers', this asks for the letters that hold each word in, its first and last

parts.note: first and last letters
first and last letters
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Bottles to carry tasty tea and fermented tea drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Containers' does double work: it is the definition and also signals the outer letters, which contain each word. Assam is an Indian black tea; kombucha is a fermented tea drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Flasks are bottles or vacuum vessels used to hold and carry drinks such as tea.
